# Phase 1: Core Syntax {.sdaia-dark background-color="#00C9A7"}

Back to Basics: Variables and Pins

## The Arduino Skeleton 💀

Every Arduino program (sketch) needs two functions:

```cpp
void setup() {
  // Runs ONCE when the robot turns on.
  // Used to set up pins, start serial, etc.
}

void loop() {
  // Runs FOREVER, over and over again.
  // This is where the main logic lives!
  // Note: Code runs line by line until finished, then restarts the loop from the beginning.
}
```

## Talking to Pins 🔌

From Session 1, we learned that pins can be `OUTPUT` (like LEDs or Motors) or `INPUT` (like Sensors).

```cpp
const int ledPin = 9;

void setup() {
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);
  Serial.begin(9600); // Start talking to computer
}

void loop() {
  digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH); // Turn ON (5V)
  delay(1000);                // Wait 1 sec
  digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW);  // Turn OFF (0V)
  delay(1000);
}
```


# Phase 2: Functions & Movement {.sdaia-dark background-color="#1C355E"}

Don't repeat yourself!

## Why Functions? 🛠️

In Session 2, we learned that writing the same motor code over and over makes our program messy. Function let us 'package' code into a single command!

:::: {.columns}
::: { .fragment .column width="50%"}
**Instead of this:**
```cpp

digitalWrite(ML_Ctrl, HIGH); 
analogWrite(ML_PWM, 150);    
digitalWrite(MR_Ctrl, HIGH); 
analogWrite(MR_PWM, 150);   

```
:::

::: {.fragment .column width="50%"}
**We write it ONCE:**
```cpp
void moveForward() {
  digitalWrite(ML_Ctrl, HIGH); 
  analogWrite(ML_PWM, 150);    
  digitalWrite(MR_Ctrl, HIGH); 
  analogWrite(MR_PWM, 150); 
}
```
:::
::::

. . .

And then just call `moveForward();` in our loop!

## Motor Setup Recap 🚗

Remember to set all motor pins as OUTPUTs!

```cpp
const int MR_Ctrl = 2; const int MR_PWM = 6;
const int ML_Ctrl = 4; const int ML_PWM = 5;

void setup() {
  pinMode(ML_Ctrl, OUTPUT); pinMode(ML_PWM, OUTPUT);
  pinMode(MR_Ctrl, OUTPUT); pinMode(MR_PWM, OUTPUT);
}
```
*Quick Quiz: Which function controls the speed?*

. . .


::: {.callout-tip}
## The Answer
`analogWrite` controls speed from 0 to 255!
:::


# Phase 3: The Senses {.sdaia-dark background-color="#E84A5F"}

Ultrasonic Sensors & Servos

## The Helper Function that Returns 🦇

In Session 3, we made a special function. It doesn't just DO something, it **gives back an answer**!

```cpp
int measureDistance() {
  // Send the sound wave
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);
  delayMicroseconds(2);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, HIGH);
  delayMicroseconds(10);
  digitalWrite(trigPin, LOW);

  // Listen for echo and do the math
  long duration = pulseIn(echoPin, HIGH);
  return duration * 0.034 / 2; // GIVES BACK the distance!
}
```

## Sweeping the Servo 🧹

We use the `<Servo.h>` library to command our radar's motor.

```cpp
#include <Servo.h>
Servo myServo;

void setup() {
  myServo.attach(10); // Servo is on pin 10
}

void loop() {
  myServo.write(0);   // Look right
  delay(500);
  myServo.write(180); // Look left
  delay(500);
  myServo.write(90);  // Look forward
  delay(500);
}
```

# Phase 4: The Autonomous Brain {.sdaia-dark background-gradient="linear-gradient(135deg, #1C355E, #00C9A7)"}

Making Choices (Session 4)

## If / Else Logic ⚖️

The core of Artificial Intelligence (and our robot) is making decisions based on data.

```cpp
int distance = measureDistance();

if (distance < 20) {
  // Danger! Path blocked!
  moveBackward();
  delay(500);
  stopMotors();
} else {
  // All clear!
  moveForward();
}
```
This single block of code is what turns a remote-controlled toy into an **Autonomous Explorer**.


# Phase 5: The Ultimate Challenge {.sdaia-dark background-color="#E84A5F"}

The "Smart Remote" Rover

## The Challenge 🏆

**Goal:** Combine Session 2 (IR Remote) and Session 4 (Obstacle Avoidance)!

Write a program where you control the robot with your IR remote (Forward, Back, Left, Right). 
**BUT**, the robot is also constantly running its `measureDistance()` function.

If you try to drive the robot into a wall, the robot must refuse the command and stop automatically!

## The Logic Flow

Inside your `loop()`:

1. Check the ultrasonic sensor (`measureDistance()`).
2. Read the IR Remote signal.
3. Is distance < 15 cm? 
   - **Yes:** If the remote says "FORWARD", ignore it and `stopMotors()`. (But allow turning or reversing!).
   - **No:** Follow the remote's commands normally.

**Good luck, Master Coders!**
